recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR-12177. If Patient Care later finalizes a separate proposal to qualify, remove, or move criticality to an extension, reconcile that later issue separately rather than changing this historical FHIR-12177 application.
issue_request: The Published DSTU2 Patient Care issue asked whether AllergyIntolerance.criticality should be removed or whether its value set should be aligned with SNOMED severity concepts. The Not Persuasive with Modification resolution directed editors to add a usage note distinguishing condition-level criticality from reaction-level severity and to make no value set change because the criticality concepts are FHIR/V3 criticality concepts rather than SNOMED severity concepts.
initial_application: Git commit f3f2ad2c4b57ba4d2dfbbd990363885b40b49101 explicitly applied GF#12177 by adding the approved AllergyIntolerance.criticality comment to the spreadsheet source. The current StructureDefinition source retains a GF#12177 committee note and includes the requested criticality/severity usage note.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists AllergyIntolerance as an active current-build resource owned by Patient Care. FHIR-8146 had earlier requested usage notes distinguishing criticality from severity. FHIR-31770 later resolved no-change for HL7 v2/SNOMED mapping guidance and confirmed there is no universal mapping from local severity to FHIR criticality. FHIR-53608 questioned the categorical wording but was Resolved - No Change/Retracted, and FHIR-54013 remains Triaged, so neither is a final applied supersession for this seed.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active AllergyIntolerance.criticality definition already contains the approved usage note, and the AllergyIntoleranceCriticality CodeSystem/ValueSet remain a FHIR criticality value set rather than a SNOMED severity binding.

related_jiras.note: Earlier published issue requested usage notes distinguishing AllergyIntolerance criticality from reaction severity.
Later no-change issue confirmed there is no global HL7 v2/SNOMED severity mapping to FHIR criticality.
Later retracted/no-change issue questioned the exact assertion but did not provide a final applied supersession.
Open triaged proposal to make criticality an extension is not a final decision for this run.
